pladdrr Documentation Convention

Source: vignettes/agents/documentation.Rmd
documentation.Rmd

Purpose: How to write roxygen2 doc blocks for the shared-dispatch-table wrapper types (Sound, Formant, Pitch, etc. — see architecture.Rmd § Dispatch Patterns). Sound (R/sound-wrapper.R) is the reference implementation; copy its shape.

Why this file exists

DESCRIPTION does not set Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE). Markdown-style doc text (- `method()` - description, backticks for code) is not processed by roxygen2 in this package — it is emitted into the .Rd file as literal text. Rd’s plain-text renderer collapses adjacent lines into a single flowed paragraph, so a hand-written bullet list renders as one run-on paragraph with literal backticks/asterisks in both ?Sound and pkgdown/HTML output. This was the root cause of the “confusing docs” report that started this convention (see git history around the Sound pilot).

Fix: write real Rd markup in the roxygen comment, not markdown. Roxygen passes @section body text through mostly unprocessed, so \itemize, \enumerate, \code{}, \url{}, \preformatted{} all work directly inside #' comments.

Doc block shape (mirror Sound) 

#' ClassName
#'
#' One-sentence description of the underlying Praat object.
#'
#' A short paragraph of detail: what it holds, what it's used for.
#' Only include a section like "File I/O" if the class actually has
#' nontrivial construction logic worth explaining.
#'
#' @section Usage:
#' \preformatted{
#' obj <- Sound$create_tone(frequency = 440, duration = 1.0)$to_pitch()
#' }
#'
#' @section Query methods:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \code{get_mean()} - mean pitch in Hz
#'   \item \code{get_minimum()}, \code{get_maximum()} - range
#' }
#'
#' @section <Other category>:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item ...
#' }
#'
#' @param .xptr Not for direct use. External pointer to the underlying C++
#'   object; set internally when a method returns a new object.
#' @return A ClassName object.
#' @usage ClassName(.xptr = NULL)
#'
#' @examples
#' pitch <- Sound$create_tone(frequency = 220, duration = 0.5)$to_pitch()
#' pitch$get_mean()
#'
#' @seealso [Sound], [Formant]
#' @name ClassName
NULL

Rules, in order of how often they’re missed:

  1. Lists are \itemize/\enumerate, never - markdown bullets. One \item per method. Method/argument names go in \code{}, not backticks.
  2. Section headers are sentence case (Query methods, not Query Methods) — Title Case in headings is an AI-writing tell, not R house style.
  3. No duplicate explanations. If a @section already explains something in detail (e.g. supported file formats), the matching @param gets one short sentence and a pointer to the section, not the same paragraph twice.
  4. Internal-only params get “Not for direct use.” Dispatch-table objects carry a .xptr (or similarly dot-prefixed) constructor arg that end users never set themselves. It still needs a documented @param (R CMD check flags undocumented arguments), but say plainly that it’s internal and what sets it — don’t let it read like a normal user-facing argument.
  5. No stale/marketing markers. Cut **NEW**, “cutting-edge”, version-bragging, or anything whose real home is history.Rmd/the changelog, not the reference doc a user opens mid-analysis. If a fact about why something exists matters, it belongs in architecture.Rmd or history.Rmd, not repeated in every method’s Rd page.
  6. Humanize the prose. No em dashes, no **bold** \n**bold** inline-header lists, no hedging/filler. Plain, direct, friendly-scientific register — write like the Sound doc reads. Run non-trivial rewrites past the humanizer skill patterns (AI Vocabulary, Overuse of Boldface, Em Dashes, Title Case in Headings are the ones that show up most in this codebase).
  7. Every exported name needs \usage. An @name class page gets no usage from roxygen, and R-devel now reports “Exported functions without usage information” for any exported function missing from \usage (INFO on R-devel r90991). A deprecated alias documented only as @usage # Deprecated: ... counts as missing, because roxygen copies that comment into \usage verbatim. Give the block @usage ClassName(args) with the real signature plus a @param for each argument, and confirm with tools::codoc(dir = "."), which must report no mismatches.

Verifying a doc block

After editing, regenerate and spot-check the specific topic — don’t just trust that roxygenise() exiting 0 means the rendered page is right, since malformed markdown-as-text degrades silently (no warning, just a run-on paragraph):

roxygen2::roxygenise()
tools::Rd2HTML("man/ClassName.Rd", out = "/tmp/ClassName.html")  # eyeball the <ul>/<ol> actually list
# or, plain-text:
# R CMD Rdconv -t txt man/ClassName.Rd | less

Confirm method-list sections render as one bullet per line (<li> per method, or • per method in text mode), not one flowed paragraph.

Vignettes and Suggests packages

A chunk that calls library() or :: on a package that is only in Suggests must be guarded, or a build without that package fails: put eval = requireNamespace("pkg", quietly = TRUE) in the chunk header (all packages the chunk uses, joined with &&), and guard every chunk that uses the package, not just the first. Check by knitting the vignette with the package masked as absent and with knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE): knitr::knit() swallows chunk errors by default, so a plain knit proves nothing. Chunks that are eval = FALSE need no guard.

Documenting validated arguments

When a method validates an argument, say what is accepted and which condition class a bad value raises (pladdrr_input_error, with $param naming the argument); do not leave it to the example. A unit or averaging_method string that an unknown value used to fall back from now errors, and the Rd must name the accepted spellings (?Ltas and ?Intensity are the model). Where a bound exists (2^29 cells), state it.

srr tags

@srrstats {ID} marks a standard as addressed and must sit beside the code, test or document that addresses it (a roxygen block ending in @noRd and NULL in an R/ file, or a #' header comment in a test file). pkgcheck runs srr:::check_standards_in_files() and fails with “standards … mostly only documented in one file” when one file holds more than half of the addressed tags, and with “only present in one directory” when R/ is the only place. @srrstatsTODO (open or partial) and @srrstatsNA (not applicable, with a reason) stay in R/srr-stats-standards.R. When a TODO is closed, move it to the file that closes it and change the tag. Check with srr:::check_standards_in_files(srr:::get_stds_from_code(normalizePath("."))), which returns "" when the spread is fine. roxygen2::roxygenise() prints the remaining TODO list.

Vignette code fences

goodpractice (extract_vignette_code) counts a chunk start as a line matching ^```\s*\{\s*r\b and a chunk end as any line matching ^```\s*$. A display-only block fenced with backticks (python, praat, bash, or no language) therefore adds an end with no start, and pkgcheck prints “Chunk start/end indices failed sanity checks in vignette.” Fence display-only blocks with ~~~ instead (leave a blank line before the opener, or pandoc will not read it as a fence). Rendering is the same. Executed code is unchanged: only {r} chunks run. Starts and ends must be equal in every vignette; a ten-line script in inst/ or dev/ that counts both is enough to check.
